Issue: Owlonius is implemented with the engine SPELLPOWER_DOUBLE tag (update = Refresh(CONTROLLER, {GameTag.SPELLPOWER_DOUBLE: 1})). In player.get_spell_damage the result is computed as (amount + spellpower) << spellpower_double, which doubles the ENTIRE spell-damage figure including the spell's base damage. With Owlonius on board (Spell Damage +1) a 6-damage Fireball deals (6+1)<<1 = 14.
Real behaviour: Owlonius reads 'Your spells get double bonus from Spell Damage' â€” only the bonus from Spell Damage is doubled, not the base damage. With +1 Spell Damage the bonus becomes +2, so a 6-damage Fireball should deal 6 + 2 = 8, not 14. The SPELLPOWER_DOUBLE tag is the wrong primitive (it models Prophet-Velen-style 'double all spell damage').
Fix: d2fe8eae — TOY_807 now uses the SPELLPOWER_BONUS_DOUBLE tag and player.get_spell_damage doubles only the Spell Damage bonus, not the base; test asserts a +1 Spell Damage 6-dmg spell deals 8, not 14.

ForceDraw is a TargetedAction whose ARGS is only (TARGET,) â€” so the first positional arg CONTROLLER becomes TARGET (the Player) and the RANDOM(FRIENDLY_DECK + MINION) selector is silently ignored. Two consequences verified at runtime: (1) the draw is NOT restricted to minions â€” with only a spell (Moonfire) in deck it draws the spell; (2) `ForceDraw.TARGET` resolves to the Player, so `Find(Player + PIRATE)` is always empty and the Coin is NEVER granted even when the drawn card is a Pirate (drew Southsea Deckhand -> 0 Coins).
Real behaviour: Draw a minion (minion-restricted). If the drawn minion is a Pirate, get a Coin (GAME_005). Likely fix: use a draw action that draws a specific minion target and exposes the drawn card as its TARGET (e.g. Draw(CONTROLLER, RANDOM(FRIENDLY_DECK + MINION)) or a Dredge-style minion draw), then gate the Coin on Find(<drawncard> + PIRATE).
Fix: eea8ccbf — Draw(player,selector) (not ForceDraw, which drops the selector): minion-restricted draw + Coin gates on the drawn card being a Pirate

Issue: The effect is scripted as `play = Draw(...).then(Buff(...))` on a Location card. Locations should script their effect under `activate =`, which fires only on use(). Because UseLocation falls back to running the `play` script when no `activate` exists, the draw fires BOTH at play time AND on each subsequent use(). Verified: after loc.play() a battlecry minion is already drawn into hand with -1 cost; using the location later draws a second one. Net effect: one extra free draw the printed card never grants, and the play-time draw breaks the Location's intended deferred-charge semantics.
Real behaviour: Fairy Tale Forest is a 3-Cost Location with 3 charges. It does nothing when played; each USE draws a Battlecry minion that costs (1) less. The fix is to rename the script attribute from `play` to `activate` so the engine only runs it on use().
Fix: 5106a84f — script moved from play to activate so the discounted Battlecry-minion draw fires on Location use(), not on play; test asserts no draw on play and a draw on use.

Issue: Cleave is wired as events = Attack(SELF).on(CLEAVE) where CLEAVE = Hit(TARGET_ADJACENT, ATK(SELF)). TARGET_ADJACENT = ADJACENT(TARGET) and TARGET = source.target. The Deathrattle (Hit(ENEMY_CHARACTERS, 2)) works correctly.

Fix: eea8ccbf — CLEAVE now reads ATTACK_TARGET_ADJACENT (defender lives in source.attack_target during an attack), fixing all cleave-on-attack minions

Issue: _SummonTwoDeathrattleFight summons two deathrattle minions then issues TWO separate Attack() calls (Attack(a,b) followed by Attack(b,a)), each gated only on both still being in PLAY. Each Attack() is already a full bidirectional combat exchange (Attack.do queues Hit(defender, attacker.atk) AND the retaliation Hit(attacker, defender.atk)). So when neither minion dies after the first exchange, the second Attack runs a SECOND full exchange and each minion takes its opponent's attack TWICE. Verified empirically: two 2/3 Harvest Golems each receive 4 damage (4 Hit events) and BOTH die.
Real behaviour: Battlecry: Summon two Deathrattle minions from your deck. They fight! - 'They fight!' is a single combat exchange: each minion deals its Attack to the other once. Two 2/3 minions should end at 2/1 each and both survive; only when one minion's attack >= the other's health does a minion die. The existing test (two 2/1 Leper Gnomes) masks the bug because both die on the first exchange, so the in-PLAY gate skips the second Attack.
Fix: 3f327269 - 'They fight!' now a single simultaneous strike (Hit each by other's Attack), not 2 sequential Attacks

Issue: Buff(ENEMY_HAND + MINION, 'TLC_439e') applies the +2 cost only to enemy minions currently in hand at cast time. Minions the opponent draws on their next turn are not taxed. The TLC_439e enchant expires on OWN_TURN_END of the enemy (its controller), which matches 'next turn'.
Real behaviour: Deal 2 damage to all enemy minions. Enemy minions cost (2) more next turn. - the cost increase applies to the opponent's minions during their next turn, including minions drawn/created next turn, not just those already in hand when the spell resolves.

Issue: play Discovers a Fel spell, then on Play(OWNER) of the discovered card it presents a GenericChoice of TWO freshly-generated random Fel spells (RandomSpell(spell_school=FEL) * 2). The leftover options from the original Discover are not retained; the second pick is re-rolled from the whole Fel-spell pool. Also acknowledged in the code comment as an 'approximation of pick one of the others'.
Real behaviour: Printed: 'Discover a Fel spell. If you play it this turn, also pick one of the others.' The 'others' are specifically the two Fel spells you did NOT pick from the original 3-card Discover, not two new random Fel spells. Matches the set-wide 'un-enumerated discover pools' approximation.

Issue: Battlecry requires REQ_MINION_TARGET + REQ_ENEMY_TARGET only and deals Hit(TARGET, 6); the 'with a minion type' restriction is dropped (acknowledged in the code comment, because REQ_TARGET_WITH_RACE needs a specific race param). A raceless enemy minion (e.g. Chillwind Yeti) can therefore be targeted.
Real behaviour: Printed: 'Battlecry: Deal 6 damage to an enemy minion with a minion type.' The target must have at least one minion type; minions with no race (e.g. Yeti, Boulderfist Ogre) should not be valid targets.

Issue: Token always carries a stored minion (jarred by Entomologist Toru) and its deathrattle releases it. The conditional deathrattle text is not modelled: data card has 'Deathrattle: Release nothing. (It's just an empty jar.)@Deathrattle: Release {5}!' - the server-resolved {5} (the stored minion's name) and the empty-jar variant are display-only and not rendered.
Real behaviour: Printed deathrattle dynamically shows the stored minion's name ('Release <Minion>!') or, if empty, 'Release nothing. (It's just an empty jar.)'. Functional behaviour (release the stored minion) is correct; only the {5}-magnitude / empty-variant text rendering is approximated.

Issue: play summons the replacement BEFORE destroying the target: (Summon(Controller(TARGET), RandomMinion(cost=COST(TARGET))), Destroy(TARGET)). COST(TARGET) is read before the destroy so the cost is correct, but the replacement is placed on the board while the original still occupies its slot, then the original is destroyed.
Real behaviour: Printed: "Destroy a minion. Summon a random minion of the same Cost to replace it." The live card destroys first, then summons the replacement into the freed position. Cost and net board count match; only the summoned minion's board position can differ (replacement appears beside the original rather than in its vacated slot), and a full-board edge case could in principle behave differently since the summon happens before the destroy frees a slot.

Issue: Modeled as a refund-after-pay: the Beast is played at full cost, then min(cost,2) mana is refunded via SpendMana(target,-refund) (see _ConsumeNextBeastDiscount / _NextBeastDiscount in hunter.py L8-46). This requires affording the full price first; it cannot enable a play you could not otherwise afford (e.g. 7 mana available + a 8-cost Beast with the 2-discount is unplayable here, but should be playable in HS). It also bumps refunded mana back into the pool rather than lowering the card's displayed cost.
Real behaviour: Printed: "The next Beast you play this turn costs (2) less." A genuine cost reduction lowers the Beast's cost before payment, so an 8-cost Beast becomes castable with only 6 mana.

Issue: Shuffles ten copies of UNG_920t2 ("Carnassa's Brood", the original Un'Goro token) rather than a TLC-named Raptor token. Stats and text are identical (1-Cost 3/2 Beast, "Battlecry: Draw a card"), so behaviour matches exactly; only the token's printed name differs.
Real behaviour: Printed: "Shuffle ten 1-Cost 3/2 Raptors into your deck with \"Battlecry: Draw a card.\"" The shuffled bodies are named Raptors, not Carnassa's Brood.

Issue: Shipped as a vanilla 7/7/7 body. The printed card grafts a random Titan-ability battlecry (one of 35 unscripted 7/7/7 tokens TLC_452t1..t35) onto Osk while in hand, re-rolling each turn, firing that battlecry when played. The token battlecries are not scripted, so Osk has no battlecry at all. Already self-documented in the script and review.csv.

Issue: Quest reward ships as a plain 0/8/3 weapon body with no triggered effect. The 'After you Discover a card, this plays the other (un-chosen) options. Lose 1 Durability.' effect is not modelled - discovering does nothing extra and durability never drains. Already self-documented in the script and review.csv.

Issue: play = _PrimalfinArm(CONTROLLER) only sets player.next_kindred_double = 1. Grep confirms next_kindred_double is set here but read NOWHERE in the engine or any card script: no Kindred bonus (TLC_107/243/429/454/829 etc.) consumes or doubles on it. The flag is also never cleared. So the battlecry is effectively a no-op 4/4.
Real behaviour: Printed: 'Battlecry: Your next Kindred triggers twice.' The next Kindred minion you play whose Kindred condition is met should resolve its Kindred bonus a second time.

Issue: _PterrordaxSteal does Hit(m, 1) on every other minion (dealing 1 DAMAGE, healable / triggers damage events / leaves max_health intact) then buffs the Pterrordax +1 Health per minion hit. Test asserts a 4/5 Yeti ends at health 4 (damaged), max_health still 5.
Real behaviour: Printed: 'steals 1 Health from all other minions.' The referenced enchant TLC_831e 'Pterrified | Reduced Health.' shows the canonical effect permanently REDUCES each other minion's Health (lowers max Health by 1), not deal removable damage.

Issue: play = Summon(CONTROLLER, 'TLC_100t1') always crafts the Un'Goro Jungle location; the 'deck started with 10 cards of different Costs' deckbuilding precondition is never checked (acknowledged in code comment).
Real behaviour: Printed: 'Battlecry: If your deck started with 10 cards of different Costs, craft a custom location.' The location should only be crafted when the deckbuilding constraint was met, and the location is 'custom' (built from those cards), not a fixed basic body.

Issue: play = Draw(CONTROLLER) * 2 draws two arbitrary cards. No attempt to draw a Kindred card plus a card that activates it (acknowledged in code comment).

Issue: play iterates self.controller.graveyard front-to-back (oldest death first) and triggers the first 5 minions with deathrattles. Selection order is implementation-defined rather than matching the client's death ordering.

Issue: There is no tests/test_tlc_paladin.py and no test file references any paladin TLC id (TLC_240/241/426/428/430/438/441/442/444/477). Issue: Modeled as a never-finishing quest (no progress_total, no AddProgress, no QUEST_REWARD reveal): quest = Summon(CONTROLLER, MURLOC).after(_GolakkaSummon(Summon.CARD)). _GolakkaSummon manually counts murlocs in batches of 5 and stacks a +N/+N Buff (TLC_426e2) on each murloc summoned after each completion. Issue: "While this is alive, you get a 2-Cost Holy spell..." is modeled as a one-shot battlecry-style Give of TLC_241t on play (with _IdoStamp recording the token) plus a deathrattle _IdoRemove that discards the token only if it is still in HAND. It is not a true continuous aura: if the token leaves hand and returns, or Ido is bounced/copied, the give-once/remove-once bookkeeping can desync (e.g. token persists after Ido dies if it was not in hand at death, or a second Ido does not re-grant).
Real behaviour: While this is alive, you get a 2-Cost Holy spell that gives a minion +2/+2 and Divine Shield. (Token: Call the Threshfleet!, stays in hand while Ido is alive.)

Card: Sol'etos, Life's Breath / Sol'etos, Death's Touch
Issue: Both reward halves implement only their own listed effect. TLC_817t3 just summons a copy of itself (Battlecry) and TLC_817t4 just runs its 5-damage Deathrattle. If you're holding both halves of Sol'etos, combine!" Holding both halves should fuse them into TLC_817t5 Sol'etos, Cycle's Rebirth. Issue: play = Hit(TARGET, _TimesShuffled()) deals damage equal ONLY to the number of cards shuffled into your deck, with no base floor. Card: Master Dusk (Way of the Shell hero power)
Issue: The Lie in Wait reward summons the Master Dusk hero (TLC_513t), which equips hero power TLC_513hp 'Way of the Shell' from data. TLC_513hp has no script (get_script_definition returns None) and no generic handler, so using it draws 0 cards (verified live: hero power use() drew 0). The hero power's effect is unimplemented. Only reachable after completing the 5-shuffle quest, so low impact.

Issue: play = _CultistMapDiscoverDeck(CONTROLLER) Discovers a card from your own deck and draws the real copy out. The secondary clause is not modelled (acknowledged in the docstring/review).
Real behaviour: Printed: "Discover a card from your deck. If you play it this turn, also pick one of the others." The conditional 'play it this turn -> pick one of the other two offered cards' upside is omitted.

Issue: The global Shuffle.do wrapper bumps target._tlc_times_shuffled by the number of cards that actually entered target.deck, on ANY shuffle into that player's deck (regardless of source/controller). It also counts per card shuffled (Interrogation's 3 ninjas = +3), not per shuffle event.

Issue: Kindred attaches enchant TLC_223e (GameTag.SPELLPOWER:2) to the drawn Fire spell while it sits in HAND. The engine's spell-damage path (Player.get_spell_damage) only sums board-level spellpower from minions in PLAY (self.spellpower / self.spellpower_fire); a SPELLPOWER tag on a card in hand is never read. So the Kindred bonus has zero effect on the spell's damage. The unit test (test_volcanic_thrasher_kindred_active) only asserts 'TLC_223e in drawn.buffs' rather than the actual +2 damage, masking the bug (the CLAUDE.md 'assert nothing' anti-pattern).
Real behaviour: Printed: 'Battlecry: Draw a Fire spell. Kindred: Give it Spell Damage +2.' The drawn spell should deal +2 damage when cast. Verified at runtime: with Kindred active, the drawn Fireball dealt 6 damage (its base) instead of 8 - the +2 Spell Damage is silently lost.
Fix: 3f327269 - engine get_spell_damage now reads the cast spell's own SPELLPOWER enchant; Kindred +2 applies at cast

Card: Spirit of the Mountain / Ashalon, Ridge Guardian
Issue: reward = Summon(CONTROLLER, 'TLC_229t14') summons Ashalon, but TLC_229t14 has no script class anywhere in the_lost_city package (grep confirms only the Summon reference exists). Ashalon enters as a vanilla 8/8 Elemental/Beast with no battlecry. This is the 'quest-reward payoff that summons a vanilla body' set-wide approximation.

Issue: play = (Hit(RANDOM_ENEMY_CHARACTER, 3), Summon(CONTROLLER, SIZZLING_CINDER) * 3). Hit() routes through source.get_damage -> get_spell_damage, so the damage scales with Spell Damage (e.g. 4 with +1 SP), but the number of Sizzling Cinders summoned is hardcoded at exactly 3. 'Summon that many' should equal the damage actually dealt.
Real behaviour: Printed: 'Deal $3 damage. Summon that many 2/1 Sizzling Cinders.' With Spell Damage +N the card deals 3+N and summons 3+N cinders; the impl always summons 3. Exact only when board Spell Damage is 0.

Issue: play = _MountainMapDiscover(...).then(Give(...)) resolves only the primary Discover. The 'If you play it this turn, also pick one of the others' follow-up Discover is not modeled (acknowledged in the card's own comment).

Issue: 'Your Elementals deal 1 extra damage' is modeled as a +1 Attack aura (Refresh ... {GameTag.ATK:1}) on friendly Elementals, because no card-reachable outgoing-damage hook exists. Acknowledged in the card comment.
Real behaviour: Printed: 'Your Elementals deal 1 extra damage.' Real card raises only damage dealt (combat AND effect damage) without raising displayed Attack. The aura raises displayed Attack and does not cover an Elemental's spell/effect damage.

Issue: Implemented as GenericChoice over RANDOM(FRIENDLY_DECK + MINION) * 3. GenericChoice.choose() discards every presented card that wasn't chosen. Because the three presented cards are real deck-minion instances, the two un-chosen options are pulled out of the deck and DISCARDED. Verified live: a 31-minion deck dropped to 28 after one cast (1 to hand + 2 silently milled).
Real behaviour: "Discover a minion from your deck. Make it Temporary." A deck-Discover removes ONLY the chosen card from the deck (to hand); the two unchosen options stay in the deck. The card should not thin the deck by 3.
Fix: 3f327269 - proper deck-Discover (ForceDraw the chosen id); non-chosen deck cards no longer discarded

Issue: Reward gives TLC_446t1 to hand, and TLC_446t1 is scripted as a one-shot spell-like play (_UnderfelRiftActivate): on play it discards one random card and immediately summons 2 Fel Beasts, then is gone. In data TLC_446t1 is a MINION (HEALTH 1) that persists on the board.
Real behaviour: "Select the Rift to activate. Throw a card in to summon 2 random Fel Beasts. (Once per turn.)" Underfel Rift is a persistent board entity (Location-style minion) you activate once per turn each turn, throwing in a card each time. The impl collapses it into a single activation with no persistence, no per-turn cooldown, and no board body.

Issue: The host enchantment's aura (Refresh(FRIENDLY_HAND + TEMPORARY, COST: -2)) discounts ALL Temporary cards held in hand simultaneously, not just one. Net gameplay is correct (the host is destroyed on the first Temporary play, so only one discount is ever consumed), but if you hold two Temporary cards both visually show the -2 until one is played.
Real behaviour: "Your next Temporary card costs (2) less." Only the single next Temporary card should display/receive the discount.

Issue: Battlecry gives 2 random UNG quest-reward tokens via Give(CONTROLLER, RandomEntourage()) * 2, but the printed 'Shuffle the rest into your deck' clause is not modelled (the remaining 7 rewards are never shuffled in). Documented in an in-code comment.
Real behaviour: Printed (live data TLC_602t): 'Battlecry: Get 2 random "Journey to Un'Goro" Quest Rewards. Shuffle the rest into your deck.' - the 7 unchosen rewards should be shuffled into the player's deck.

Issue: play = Kindred() & Hit(OUTERMOST(ENEMY_MINIONS), 6). The Kindred() evaluator gates the 6-damage effect on/off via kindred_active() but never consults Player.next_kindred_double. That flag is set by Primalfin Challenger (the_lost_city/neutral.py _PrimalfinChallenger -> target.next_kindred_double = 1) yet is never read or decremented by ANY Kindred card, including this one.
Real behaviour: With Primalfin Challenger active, 'your next Kindred triggers twice', so an active Kindred on Diabolus Rex should deal 6 damage to the outermost enemy minions TWICE (12 total to each of left/right-most). Current impl always triggers the Kindred bonus exactly once. This is the set-wide 'Kindred-doubling' approximation named in the brief; recorded here as it concretely affects DINO_138. No crash; tests don't cover the Primalfin-Challenger interaction.

Issue: _SaucierDiscount does not capture the Saucier's physical neighbours at play time. It runs in the battlecry (after the Saucier has already left hand) and reconstructs neighbours heuristically: it scans the post-removal hand for cards whose engine-wide adjacent_plays_this_turn counter advanced since a per-card _saucier_adj_seen snapshot, then takes the first contiguous run (1 or 2 cards) of freshly-bumped indices and buffs those with DINO_137e (COST -1).
Real behaviour: Reduce the Cost of the (immediate left/right) adjacent cards in your hand by (1). The heuristic leans on the shared GDB 'Orbital' adjacent_plays_this_turn counter and a contiguous-run + break assumption. The two provided tests (middle slot, left-edge slot) pass and the delta-snapshot guards against stale earlier-play bumps, so likely correct in common cases, but the reconstruction is indirect rather than capturing neighbours directly in Play.do; worth a defensive test for multi-play-in-one-turn boards where a non-neighbour was bumped by an earlier play and a neighbour run is split by the break.

Issue: The in-hand Mirrex is modelled by Morph-ing the card into the full copied minion (e.g. Boulderfist Ogre CS2_200) plus the DINO_407e2 'Crystalline' enchant that pins stats to 3/3. Because it becomes the actual minion card, the copy inherits the copied minion's MANA COST: verified live, after the opponent plays a 6-cost Boulderfist Ogre the Mirrex copy in hand reports cost == 6 (printed 'Mirrex base cost: 3' -> 'copy id: CS2_200 cost: 6'). The DINO_407e2 enchant only sets stats (atk/max_health lambdas = 3), never cost.
Real behaviour: Printed: 'While in your hand, this is a 3/3 copy of the last minion your opponent played.' In Hearthstone an in-hand transform-into-copy of this kind keeps the copying card's own cost (Mirrex stays a 3-mana 3/3 with the copied minion's text/abilities). Crystalline = '3/3' is the only stat-pinning enchant in data; there is no cost-setting enchant, indicating the cost should remain Mirrex's 3, not the copied minion's. Falls under the known set-wide 'Mirrex in-hand continuous transform' approximation, but the inherited cost is a concrete behavioural divergence (cheats out an expensive body for full price instead of 3).

Issue: The impl marks the reflecting state with a Python _mirrex attribute and never applies the data enchant DINO_407e 'Reflecting' ('Transforming into the last minion your opponent plays.'). It does apply DINO_407e2 'Crystalline'. So the cosmetic 'Reflecting' enchant/text is absent.
Real behaviour: The real card carries the DINO_407e 'Reflecting' defining enchantment while in hand. Purely cosmetic/engine-model; no gameplay effect, the behavioural copy is driven correctly by the Play.do + Hand.update hooks.

Card: Bwonsamdi / Boon of Power / Boon of Longevity / Boon of Speed
Issue: Bwonsamdi's deathrattle (TIME_619t) is hardcoded to Summon(CONTROLLER, RandomMinion(cost=4)). Each Boon (_apply_boon) bumps card._bwonsamdi_boon_cost by 2, but a repo-wide grep shows that attribute is only ever written (deathknight.py:141-142) and asserted in a test (test_timeways_deathknight.py:286) -- it is never read by the deathrattle or anywhere else. So the summoned minion stays in the 4-Cost bracket no matter how many Boons were given; the 'cost (2) more' / 'carry over' clause is dead state.
Real behaviour: Bwonsamdi: 'Deathrattle: Summon a random @-Cost minion. (Any Boons given to Bwonsamdi carry over.)' base @=4. Each Boon: 'Minions summoned by his Deathrattle cost (2) more.' so with N boons the summon should draw from the (4+2N)-Cost bracket (1 boon -> 6, 2 -> 8).
Fix: 2a80d756 — _BwonsamdiDeathrattle reads _bwonsamdi_boon_cost; summons RandomMinion(cost=4+2N)

Issue: _HuskHeroDeathrattle only spends min(20, corpses) Corpses; it does not resurrect the dead hero nor set the hero's Health to the amount spent. Reviving a dead hero is an engine limitation, so corpse-spend is the only observable effect. The data tokens TIME_618e2 'A Second Chance' (resurrection marker) and TIME_618t 'Eternal Life' (the granted deathrattle spell) exist in data but are not wired anywhere in code (confirmed by grep).
Real behaviour: Battlecry: Give your hero "Deathrattle: Spend up to 20 Corpses to resurrect with that much Health."
Fix: Accepted engine limitation: resurrecting a dead hero is unsupported; corpse-spend is the only observable effect. Data tokens TIME_618e2/TIME_618t remain inert.

Issue: Script plays Hit(RANDOM(ENEMY_MINIONS), 3). The data has no REQ_TARGET / no targeting tags, so 'Deal $3 damage' is untargeted -- in Hearthstone an untargeted 'Deal X damage' hits a random ENEMY CHARACTER (hero included). By restricting to ENEMY_MINIONS the 3 damage never hits the enemy hero and fizzles entirely on an empty enemy board. Engine precedent for untargeted random damage in this very set uses RANDOM(ENEMY_CHARACTERS) (warlock.py:200).
Real behaviour: Deal $3 damage (to a random enemy, hero included). Freeze two random enemy minions.
Fix: 2a80d756 — $3 Hit selector ENEMY_MINIONS -> ENEMY_CHARACTERS (hero now in pool)

Issue: _ChronochillerSkipDraw sets cant_draw=True at OWN_TURN_BEGIN and _ChronochillerRestoreDraw clears it at OWN_TURN_END. player.draw() (player.py:964) early-returns whenever cant_draw is set, so EVERY draw the controller makes during their turn is suppressed, not only the start-of-turn draw. A same-turn extra-draw effect played while Chronochiller is in play would be wrongly cancelled. Self-documented as an approximation.
Real behaviour: You no longer draw a card at the start of your turn (only the start-of-turn draw should be cancelled).
Fix: 2a80d756 — OWN_TURN_BEGIN sets player.skip_next_start_draw; engine skips only the one start draw

Issue: play = Hit(RANDOM_ENEMY_CHARACTER, 4) * 2 multiplies the ACTION, so the RANDOM_ENEMY_CHARACTER selector is re-evaluated independently for each of the two 4-damage hits (engine loops get_targets() per iteration in TargetedAction.trigger). With 2+ enemies it can roll the same target twice (8 damage to one, 0 to another) and does not guarantee two distinct enemies. The codebase convention for 'two random enemies' multiplies the SELECTOR via random.sample (RandomSelector.eval), giving two distinct targets in one shot: classic/demonhunter.py:87 Hit(RANDOM_ENEMY_MINION * 2, 2), classic/hunter.py:89, classic/shaman.py:160, classic/warrior.py:108 all use selector*2 for printed text 'two random enemy minions'. The Action*2 form (Hit(RANDOM_ENEMY_CHARACTER, N) * 2) is only used for Ragnaros-style repeat-hit hero powers (blackrock 'DIE, INSECTS!', brawl mechwar) that are MEANT to re-roll. Should be Hit(RANDOM(ENEMY_CHARACTERS - DEAD) * 2, 4).
Real behaviour: Rewind / Deal $4 damage to two random enemies (two distinct enemies).
Fix: 04d6f336 — Hit(RANDOM_ENEMY_CHARACTER*2,4): two distinct random enemies

Issue: Data TIME_446e (Jailbreak) is a global AURA (AURA:1) whose printed text is 'Your next minion costs (0)' — a discount on the next minion the player plays. The script instead applies COST:-100 directly to the specific Demon just obtained from the location (Buff(given_demon, 'TIME_446e')). If the player plays a different minion first, or never plays the obtained demon, the real card's 'next minion played = 0' discount is not modeled; only the acquired demon is discounted. Not covered by any CONTEXT exemption (not Rewind, not a scaling magnitude, not a Discover pool).
Real behaviour: Get a Demon that costs (5) or more. If your deck has no minions, your next one costs (0).
Fix: 2a80d756 — sets player.next_minion_costs_zero (deck has no minions) instead of buffing the obtained Demon

Card: Lady Azshara (Empower the Well) / The Well of Eternity (TIME_211t1t)
Issue: The empowered Well (_FillTemporarySpells doubled=True) marks each generated spell with Buff(spell, "TIME_211t1te") (Eternalized). In data TIME_211t1te carries only CARD_SET/CLASS/CARDTYPE tags (no SPELLS_CAST_TWICE or any mechanical tag — verified via cardxml), and the script registers it as a bare no-op class. The engine's spell-double-cast is keyed solely on the player-wide aura flag player.spells_cast_twice (actions.py:1897 has_extra_battlecries) plus the relic-specific next_relic_casts_twice; there is NO per-spell/per-enchant double-cast path. So spells produced by the empowered Well get a no-op marker and cast only once — the defining 'cast twice' effect of the Empower-the-Well branch is missing. Real behaviour: Empower the Well: 'The spells created by The Well of Eternity will cast twice. Destroy Zin-Azshari.' / empowered Well: 'Fill your hand with random Temporary spells. They cast twice.'
Fix: 04d6f336 — per-spell _casts_twice_self flag; empowered Well sets it; engine doubles cast

Issue: Battlecry casts the stored _taught_spell correctly, but the printed text 'Cast {0}.' placeholder is never filled — no custom_cardtext / CUSTOM_CARDTEXT tag wiring on TIME_704t (the cards in this same package, e.g. paladin.py, do use custom_cardtext, so the pattern exists and was simply not applied here). The card text renders the raw {0}.
Real behaviour: Highborne Pupil battlecry text: 'Battlecry: Cast {0}.' where {0} should resolve to the taught spell's name.

Issue: _UntimelyResummon gates only on `target.turn_played >= source.game.turn` (i.e. it fires for ANY strictly-later turn). The secret-exhausted rule (card.py: a secret is suppressed while controller.current_player) already prevents it from firing on the controller's own turns, so the candidate's literal '+2'/'turn 9 own-turn' scenario can't happen — but it WAS reproduced firing on a much-later OPPONENT turn: a Chillwind Yeti played on turn 1 that survives and dies on turn 4 (opponent's turn) still revealed the secret and resummoned (secret -> GRAVEYARD, 1 fresh copy). The printed condition is only the turn IMMEDIATELY after being played, so deaths two+ turns later must NOT trigger. Confirmed over-fire: needs an upper-bound check (e.g. turn_played >= game.turn - 2), not just turn_played < game.turn.
Real behaviour: Secret: When a friendly minion dies the turn after being played, resummon it. (Only the single following turn qualifies; later-turn deaths should not fire.)
Fix: 04d6f336 — bound to turn_played+1 (only the immediately-following turn fires)

Issue: _HandCenterBonus relies only on the engine's play_left_most/play_right_most boolean snapshot (actions.py 815-816) and never records the card's hand index, so it can only confirm 'center' for original hand sizes 1 and 3. Reproduced: with Precise Shot genuinely dead-center at index 2 of a 5-card hand it deals 3, not 5. The 3/5 magnitudes are both in data (not a server-scaling unknown), so the miss is a real functional gap on the common 5/7-card dead-center play, not an accepted @-scaling approximation. Documented in-code as an engine-snapshot limitation.
Real behaviour: Deal 3 damage. If this is EXACTLY in the center of your hand, deal 5 instead.
Fix: 2a80d756 — _HandCenterBonus uses _play_hand_index/_play_hand_size; exact center for any hand size

Issue: play = (Silence(RANDOM(ENEMY_MINIONS)), Destroy(RANDOM(ENEMY_MINIONS))) rolls RANDOM(ENEMY_MINIONS) twice independently, so with 2+ enemy minions on board it can Silence one minion and Destroy a different one. The Silence is meant to strip the destroyed minion's deathrattle; silencing a different minion than the one destroyed defeats the card's purpose.
Real behaviour: "Rewind. Silence and destroy a random enemy minion." — one minion is chosen at random, then both Silenced and Destroyed. The codebase's correct idiom (perils_in_paradise/neutral.py:90) captures the random card once and reuses it: Silence(card), Destroy(card).

Issue: _ShapeshifterMorph runs Morph(SELF, chosen.id) on the OWN_TURN_BEGIN Hand event with NO re-application of any trigger-carrying enchant. After the first morph the in-hand entity becomes a fresh card of the rolled minion's id and loses TIME_876's Hand.events, so it never re-transforms. The card transforms exactly once, not every turn. The codebase already has the correct Zerus-style pattern (Showdown WW_337/WW_337t/WW_337e): the re-transform trigger must be carried by an enchant re-applied via .then(Buff(Morph.CARD, ...)). TIME_876e exists but is never applied, confirming the gap.

Issue: King Llane's 'Start of Game: Hide from Garona in the enemy's deck' (data tag START_OF_GAME_KEYWORD=968) is explicitly not modeled (comment in TIME_875t; only play=Draw,Shuffle is scripted). The engine does support start-of-game effects via GameStart() events (precedent: emerald_dream _HamuulStartOfGame), but King Llane wires none. King Llane is a non-collectible token and nothing else summons/gives it (grep finds only Garona's check + its own def), so _GaronaBattlecry's `next(c for c in opp.hand if c.id=='TIME_875t')` never finds him in normal play and Garona's destroy + cut-Health-in-half never fires. The signature interaction of this bundle is inert.
Real behaviour: King Llane: Start of Game: Hide from Garona in the enemy's deck. Battlecry: Draw a card. Shuffle this back into your deck. Garona: Battlecry: If your opponent is holding King Llane, destroy him and cut their Health in half.
Fix: Accepted: King Llane is a non-collectible token never placed in the enemy deck in normal play (start-of-game hide is out of scope), so the interaction is inert and unobservable.

Issue: The discount enchant's `update = Refresh(FRIENDLY_HAND + RAFAAM, {GameTag.COST: -3})` applies the -3 discount to EVERY Rafaam in hand simultaneously, and the discount is only consumed (enchant destroyed) when one Rafaam is actually played via the Play(CONTROLLER, RAFAAM) event hook. Net effect (a single 3-mana discount realized) is correct, but if the player holds multiple Rafaams, all of them visibly cost 3 less until one is played, rather than only the next one.
Real behaviour: Battlecry: The next Rafaam you play costs (3) less.
Fix: Accepted net-correct: the -3 discount is realized exactly once (consumed when the next Rafaam is played); only the visual over-display on multiple held Rafaams differs. A 'left-most only' selector fix would desync display vs the play-order consume.

Issue: The opponent's two lowest-Cost cards are relocated into the opponent's hand by directly setting zones (SETASIDE -> controller swap -> HAND), bypassing the draw pipeline. This skips draw-related triggers/fatigue/overdraw-burn semantics that a real draw would invoke for the opponent (your own 2 highest are drawn via ForceDraw, which is correct). Overdraw is approximated via card.discard() when the opponent's hand is full, but it is not a true draw.
Real behaviour: Battlecry: You draw your 2 highest Cost cards. Your opponent draws your 2 lowest Cost cards.
Fix: Accepted net-correct: opponent relocation bypasses the draw pipeline (no opponent draw-trigger/fatigue/overdraw-burn) but the net hand state is exact; cross-player 'opponent draws YOUR cards' through the real draw pipeline is an engine limitation.

Issue: update doubles Battlecries/Deathrattles (EXTRA_BATTLECRIES + EXTRA_DEATHRATTLES) and re-runs the Hero Power via Activate(FRIENDLY_HERO_POWER).after(PlayHeroPower), but the 'end of turn effects trigger twice' clause is NOT implemented. There is no general engine hook to double OWN_TURN_END triggers, so end-of-turn effects fire only once. Acknowledged in the script comment.
Real behaviour: Your Battlecries, Deathrattles, Hero Power, and end of turn effects trigger twice.
Fix: Accepted: Battlecry/Deathrattle/Hero Power doubling is implemented; no general engine hook exists to double OWN_TURN_END triggers, so only the end-of-turn clause is unmodeled.

Issue: Implemented as a vanilla 3/4/3 with `pass`. Issue: cost_mod uses _EnemyHeroDamageThisTurn(), which reads opp.hero_damage_taken_this_turn. That counter accumulates damage POINTS (actions.py:1825 `+= amount`), not the number of damage events. A single 7-damage hit reduces cost by 7 instead of by 1, since the engine has no per-instance damage-event counter. Acknowledged in the docstring.

Issue: _ResetCosts applies an additive delta cost buff (delta = card.data.cost - card.cost) to every card in both hands. This correctly restores ordinary additive cost modifiers, but cannot reverse a set-to-0 effect (COST:-100): once the live cost clamps to 0, delta=base and the new raw cost = (base-100)+base may still be <=0, leaving the card at 0 instead of its original cost. Edge case to watch.
Real behaviour: Battlecry: Set the Cost of every card in both player's hands back to their original Costs.
Fix: 2a80d756 — _ResetCosts two-stage: strips pure cost-only enchants (reverses COST:-100 set-to-0) then applies residual additive delta

Issue: END_012 sets GameTag.CANNOT_ATTACK_HEROES on the weapon entity (the data tag 321 is unmapped, so the script restores it via the mapped GameTag). But the engine's attack-target filter at card.py:1337 checks self.cannot_attack_heroes on the *attacking character* (the Hero). cannot_attack_heroes is a boolean_property (card.py:1295) that reads only the entity's own tags. The Hero class (card.py:1463) aggregates windfury/lifesteal/poisonous/has_overkill/has_honorable_kill/incoming_damage_divider/atk from its equipped weapon (card.py:1493-1541) but has NO cannot_attack_heroes property that aggregates from the weapon. Empirically verified: after equipping END_012, weapon.cannot_attack_heroes==True but hero.cannot_attack_heroes==False, the enemy hero is in hero.attack_targets, and hero.can_attack(enemy_hero)==True with atk==INFINITY. The 'Can't attack heroes' downside is fully bypassed. The script's own comment acknowledges the gap rather than patching it. The INFINITY battlecry (Buff SELF END_012e, atk=SET(2147483647)) is correct.
Real behaviour: Printed text: "[x]Can't attack heroes. Battlecry: Set this weapon's Attack to INFINITY this turn!" The 'Can't attack heroes' clause must prevent the equipped hero from attacking enemy heroes; only minions are legal targets.
Fix: e10ac8cc — Hero aggregates weapon cannot_attack_heroes (END_012 can't hit heroes)

Issue: cost_mod = -Attr(CONTROLLER, "minions_killed_this_turn") only counts the Remnant-controller's OWN minions that died this turn. Confirmed in card.py _set_zone line 1741: `self.controller.minions_killed_this_turn += 1` is bumped on the controller of the minion that DIED, so an enemy minion death increments the OPPONENT's counter, never the Remnant-controller's. Verified by running the engine: 2 enemy minions killed this turn -> p1 counter=0, p2 counter=2, game.minions_killed_this_turn (the both-sides aggregate at game.py:130-133)=2, and Remnant of Rage stayed at cost 7 instead of the expected 5. The inline comment 'covers all minions that died this turn, both sides' is false. Established precedent for the correct both-sides read exists in festival_of_legends/demonhunter.py, which explicitly sums `ctrl.minions_killed_this_turn + ctrl.opponent.minions_killed_this_turn`. The fix is to use game.minions_killed_this_turn (or Attr(CONTROLLER)+Attr(OPPONENT)).
Real behaviour: 'Costs (1) less for each minion that died this turn.' — every minion that dies this turn, from BOTH players, should reduce the cost by 1 each.
Fix: e10ac8cc — _MinionsDiedThisTurn reads game.minions_killed_this_turn (both sides)
